content_html_sanitized:
This week brought two major blasts of prohibitionist propaganda.

One came from the UN's International Narcotics Control Board's Annual Report.
From last year see
Is The UN An Instrument of Peace and Freedom Or Of War and Tyranny? UN Narks Make Answer Clear. Lies and Hatred In Service To International Police State. (International Narcotics Control Board Report)

The other was the International Narcotics Control Strategy Report -2003
Released by the Bureau for International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs in the DEAland State Department.

Somehow, I doubt if this was entirely coincidental.

The INCB is a UN/DEA bureaucracy whose job it is to monitor the various UN anti-drug treaties.
See
Swiss Government Says Going Dutch Does NOT Violate Treaties. Implications for Other Countries, Especially Canada and UK. Plus Full Text of UN Nark Press Release.

Like most bureaucracies, they view the documents that created them as ends in themselves, and no one who was not a faithful party-line prohibitionist could get a job there, anyway.

Consequently, it is hardly surprising that they are opposed to medical cannabis, anything even suggesting decriminalization, much less legalization, and also any harm reduction for hard drugs, such as safe-injection sites.

That was reported in a few Canadian papers, and denounced by The Vancouver Sun, for one. In DEAland, the story got very little play, perhaps because many people who support prohibition might be suspicious of anything involving the UN. (Rightly so.)
See
UN Nark's Speech To Swedish Prohibitionists May Cause Permanent Brain Damage. Illogic, Ignorance and Lying, Especially About the Dutch, Of Course.
and
The UN Commission on Narcotic Drugs Resolution on the Control of Cannabis in Africa. UN Narks Urge War on Poorest of the Poor. Cannabis Prohibition Does Most Damage In Poor Countries.

Statements by the US State Department were even more predictable, especially about Canada.

The Globe and Mail, one of Canada's two national newspapers, carried an article by Barrie McKenna, with reports from Todd Hurman and Colin Freeze.

CANADIAN POT A GROWING CONCERN, U.S. SAYS

WASHINGTON -- A doubling of marijuana busts on the Canada-U.S. border, along with the discovery of increasingly sophisticated growing factories, has convinced the Bush administration that the Canadian pot problem is far worse than previously thought.

The warning is contained in the U.S. State Department's annual report card on international narcotics control efforts.

While Canadian officials caution that the Americans may be reading too much into recent seizure statistics, the report released yesterday in Washington says Canada is a major source of highly potent hydroponic marijuana. It also identifies Canada as a transit-point for vast quantities of pseudoephedrine, which is used in making synthetic drugs such as methamphetamines.
See
Marijuana Bigger Problem Than Meth? DEAland And The Bush Administration Have a Very Serious Walters Problem. We Couldn't Make This Up!

Both industries are of significant and growing concern to the Bush administration because so much of the production winds up south of the border, U.S. assistant secretary of state Robert Charles said.

 " Any government which does not . . . take more seriously the production and transshipment of a schedule-1 narcotic is going to face serious follow-on questions, " Mr. Charles said.

Schedule-1 drugs are the most potent and harmful drugs classified by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Other schedule-1 narcotics include LSD and heroin.

The otherwise favourable report identified a " significant increase " in pot seizures along the Canada-U.S. border in 2003 -- 48,087 pounds ( 21,772 kilograms ), up from 26,435 pounds the previous year.

This has led the administration to conclude that " production in Canada may be higher than previously estimated, " according to the report. Without making a precise estimate of its own, the report said the increased seizures mean that the " U.S. government believes that the figure could be much higher. "

The RCMP has traditionally estimated that Canada produces roughly 800 metric tonnes of marijuana per year, but a State Department official said Canada is likely producing at least 1,000 tonnes a year. The Mounties are sticking by their estimate for the time being.

" It is an estimate. Now that estimate, while it is admittedly conservative, it is based upon the actual seizures that are made in Canada which have remained relatively constant over the last several years, " RCMP spokesman Staff Sergeant Paul Marsh said.
See
Voice of America Becomes Latest Organization to Be Corrupted By Cannabis Prohibition. Canadian Collaborators Lie To Undermine Their Country's Freedom and Sovereignty. The Myth of BC Bud.

The force hasn't yet released its 2003 statistics. The increased marijuana seizures could indicate a drastic increase in border security measures rather than a huge spike in Canadian pot production, Staff Sgt. Marsh said.

The U.S. report says Mexico remains the largest foreign supplier of marijuana to the United States.

Yes, Mexico is the largest foreign supplier, but by how much? Is Canada a close second? Hardly.

From http://www.state.gov/g/inl/rls/nrcrpt/2003/vol1/html/29833.htm
Mexico

I. Summary

The Government of Mexico (GOM) recognizes the serious threat that drug trafficking poses to national security and public safety. Mexican authorities sustained an intensive counternarcotics effort throughout 2003, including the capture of major drug cartel figures and the seizure of large quantities of illicit drugs. The Office of the Attorney General (PGR) and the Mexican Secretariat of National Defense (SEDENA) reinforced the capabilities of their institutions and identified and rooted out many instances of corruption. They conducted robust eradication of cannabis and opium poppy crops, sustaining the net reductions achieved over the past several years. Despite crop eradication,Mexico continued to produce about one-third of the heroin consumed in the United States and exported about 5,000 metric tons of marijuana to the United States.

In other words, according to the State Department, Mexico supplied five times the DEAland estimate of total Canadian production.

If Canada exported 100% of its cannabis production to DEAland, then it would still account for only 20% of the Mexican supply, by their own estimates.

And now let's compare the only hard data on the supply side, seizures.

Internal seizures in Mexico: Marijuana interdiction continued at an impressive pace, with authorities confiscating over 2,019 metric tons, over 27 percent of the potential marijuana production in 2002 (7,900 metric tons).

Internal seizures in Canada:In 2002, the last year for which we have the data, Canadian internal seizures of cannabis were only 54 metric tons, less than three percent of Mexican internal seizures.

Similarly, seizures by various DEAland agencies on the American side of the Canadian border: in 2003 -- 48,087 pounds ( 21,772 kilograms ), up from 26,435 pounds the previous year.

By comparison, in 2003 the U.S. Customs and Border Patrol made 17,716 marijuana seizures of 2.1 million pounds at the Mexican border. That means that seizures on the DEAland side of the Mexican border were at least 40 times the volume seized by the U.S. Customs and Border Patrol at the Canadian border.

Is it possible that Canadian police are far less efficient than Mexican police? Is it also possible that the U.S. Customs and Border Patrol is much less efficient at the Canadian border than they are the Mexican border?

And is it really even plausible that it is just a coincidence that internal and external seizure data differ from Canada and Mexico by roughly the same amount?

Or is it more likely that Mexican production actually supplies thirty or forty or even fifty times as much of the DEAland cannabis market by volume as does Canada?

Nonetheless, our fearless Czar has another spin on a truly pathetic new Bush regime propaganda feature, Ask the White House " described as an online interactive forum where you can submit questions to Administration officials and friends of the White House.

March 1, 2004

John Walters: Hello, I am John Walters, and I look forward to chatting about what is on your mind.
Jason, from Springfield, MO writes:

Sir: Can you report any significant progress at securing the northern and southern land borders against drug smuggling? Are large amounts of drugsstill entering the country from Canada and Mexico, and if so, what can bedone?

John P. Walters:We have had remarkable cooperation with Mexico during President Fox'sadministration. We are not only strengthening the security at our borders, but, more importantly, we are putting much greater enforcement pressure on the criminal organizations that use the border. We still have much to do, but the border is better today than it was several years ago and will continue to get better in the months ahead.

Unfortunately, Canada has become a major supplier of marijuana duringthis same period. Law enforcement cooperation has been very good, butpressure on the criminal organizations has more progress to make.
See
John Walters Testimony To The Canadian Parliament. The Public Record Or What He Would Have Said, If He Was Not Afraid of Being Asked Embarrassing Questions. The Battle for Canada.

But here is what the UN narks have to say about the supply of cannabis.

From the INCB
http://www.incb.org/e/ar/2003/incb_report_2003_3.pdf

Cultivation, production, trafficking and abuse
Narcotic drugs

330. Cannabis, the most abused drug in North America, continues to be produced in large quantities in all three countries in the region. According to estimates of the United States Government, more than 10,000 tons of cannabis herb are produced in that country; in addition, more than 5,000 tons of cannabis are smuggled into the country. Almost 40 per cent of all cannabis herb seizures reported worldwide are made in Mexico.

In other words, according to the UN, DEAland produces 10,000 tons of cannabis per year, which would make it the world's largest producer of herbal cannabis, and ten times bigger than Canada. (That would make it roughly the same amount per capita, however. Canada has a population of approximately 31 million, the US a little less than 300 million. DEAland exports only a small amount of cannabis to Canada, so it consumes virtually all of its own production, plus another 5,000 tons imported primarily from Mexico.)

Subtotal

Now let's stop and look at the numbers so far.

Despite having draconian punishments that give Canadian narks a terrible case of penal envy, DEAland produces ten times as much cannabis as Canada, and then imports at least five times Canada's total production from Mexico.

And what does this tell us about Canadian cannabis exports to the US?

The more cannabis Canada exports south, the higher DEAland cannabis consumption per capita must be, and therefore the lower Canadian cannabis consumption must be. Some Canadian narks even claim that 70% to 95% of the Canadian crop goes South.

The bottom line...

If just half the Canadian crop goes south, then Canadian cannabis consumption is just one third per capita that of DEAland. Along those lines, it is also possible that the DEAland cannabis market is vastly larger than even the official numbers. In fact, the higher the estimates used for Canadian cannabis exports, the worse the failure of prohibition must be.

Alternatively, perhaps Canadian and DEAland rates of consumption are actually comparable and only a small portion of Canadian cannabis goes south. That would be consistent with the border seizure data, and would mean that the whole BC Bud story is just prohibitionist propaganda, even more so than I have been saying.

We know that by official estimates the rabidly prohibitionist hyperpower is the world's largest producer, importer, and consumer of cannabis. This is the country that is telling Canada what its cannabis laws should be.

Why do Canadian officials so fear a debate with the perpetrators of such a disaster?

Because they are full partners in the fraud.
See
As Canada Moves Toward Some Form Of Decriminalization, Canadian Narks and Walters Escalate Lying. The New Math. Canada Replaces Mexico As Leading Supplier of Cannabis. And If You Believe That
